response.message: I've drawn a support-staff assistant on Azure: staff sign in, the app pulls the synthetic ticket and the CRM customer record (read-only), searches only approved knowledge the staff member is allowed to see, drafts a grounded answer with citations, and sends anything uncertain or sensitive to a person; refunds and CRM changes are never automated. The first local test would run this flow with synthetic tickets and scripted model replies. That checks routing, permission filtering, citations and the escalation rules, but it doesn't prove answer quality, Azure OpenAI access, identity or that anything is deployed (all still to verify in a real subscription). Do your support staff already sign in with Microsoft Entra ID, or should we treat sign-in as an open choice?

proposal.title: Azure support-staff knowledge assistant (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: the full support assistant flow on Azure, covering staff sign-in, a staff web app, an orchestration API, read-only CRM lookup, the synthetic ticket queue, an approved knowledge store and a permission-filtered search index, Azure OpenAI for drafting, a grounding/safety check, human escalation and monitoring. Assumptions: Entra ID sign-in, the region, model deployment and subscription access are all unverified and still open. The CRM connection is read-only, and the assistant has no refund or record-write path. Every component here is design-only; no native Azure generator covers this workload yet, so building it needs engineering work.

requirementDrafts.rationale: An automated refund or record change would cause direct financial or data-integrity harm.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically."
requirementDrafts.statement: The assistant must never issue refunds or create, update or delete CRM records. It only drafts, and those actions go to a person.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without per-user filtering, staff could see restricted content in drafts.
requirementDrafts.statement: Retrieval returns only approved knowledge the signed-in staff member is permitted to see. If the identity or groups are unknown, it returns nothing.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Ungrounded answers could mislead customers. Abstaining plus human escalation limits that risk.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "grounded answer drafting ... and human escalation"
requirementDrafts.statement: Each draft cites its source passages. When the evidence is insufficient, the assistant abstains and offers escalation. (Proposal: the target is to be agreed.)

Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message: The emulation didn't fail on any logic, which is good news: no test failures were reported, and the design and its no-refund, no-CRM-write rules are intact. The run was blocked because none of the supported typed contracts covers these Azure parts yet. Sign-in, App Service, Functions, AI Search and the Blob knowledge store need native generators, and the browser, ticket queue and CRM need plans for referencing or importing existing systems. That is product engineering work, not a design flaw. Swapping in the narrow Azure private-object-storage contract would only make the run look greener while removing the scope you asked for, so I'm leaving the board unchanged and nothing was mocked or validated against a real model. The reproducer is artifact c423a0f1…, revision 2, with 8 blockers. While that work is pending, we can close one real design decision: should retrieval be keyword, vector or hybrid search? Your answer decides the AI Search index setup and whether we need an embedding model deployment.
